subject: Retention addendum and temporary log retention exception for CarePath audit
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carepath.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Audits Team <audits@carepath.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Retention needs for upcoming SOC2 evidence submission

Hi Sergio,

Quick one — our external audit team has flagged an evidence gap around log and backup retention for a subset of telemetry related to patient-matching events. The auditors need a short memo from Redwood that explains: 1) current backup purge cadence and any possible 90-day extension window for archived snapshots, and 2) whether Redwood can grant a temporary log retention exception (to 18 months) specifically for auth/event logs tied to CarePath tenant IDs.

We also need an updated subprocessor list and a DPA addendum reflecting any retention carveouts. Deadline for the package is Feb 20 so we can include it in the SOC2 bundle. Attaching our audit scope for reference (carepath_audit_scope.csv).

Can you confirm feasibility and any constraints you need from our side?

Thanks,
Daniel
---
Daniel Cho
Legal Ops, CarePath
legal@carepath.ai

Attachment: carepath_audit_scope.csv (CSV)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carepath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention needs for upcoming SOC2 evidence submission

Thanks Daniel — looping in Kimberly and Rishi for legal/technical feasibility.

Short answer: we can generally support a temporary, narrowly-scoped retention exception for audit evidence, but we need to agree on precise scope, guardrails, and an addendum to the DPA. Questions from our side to speed this up:
- Which specific event types and data elements do auditors need retained (auth logs, matching events, IPs, request IDs)?
- Is the request tenant-specific (CarePath prod only) or also for staging/test tenants?
- Do you require snapshots flagged as "audit_hold" to be excluded from purge for the full 18 months or just exportable copies for auditors?

Kimberly/Rishi — can you weigh in on the maximum practical window and any compliance/legal constraints? We should aim to have a DPA addendum draft by early next week and a tech runbook that describes the deletion workflow and evidence exports.

—Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carepath.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention needs for upcoming SOC2 evidence submission

Hi all,

We can accommodate an exception but need to tighten scope and controls. High-level legal position:
- Default Redwood retention for backup snapshots and logs is 12 months in our standard DPA. Extending to 18 months is an exception and must be limited, timeboxed, and documented in a DPA addendum.
- Exception scope should be: CarePath production tenant only; event-level auth and matching logs (no application payloads or user content unless explicitly required).
- Access controls: only named auditors and Redwood SOC/Infra on a need-to-know basis; any exports must be audited and hashed.
- Subprocessors: we will produce an updated subprocessor list and mark any storage/backups handled by third parties. The addendum must include an explicit subprocessor acknowledgment clause.

I've attached an initial DPA addendum draft (DPA_Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf) that models the 90-day backup purge extension for snapshots and a targeted 18-month log retention carveout for the listed event types. Please review and propose edits.

Kimberly Park
Legal Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: DPA_Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf (PDF)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carepath.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention needs for upcoming SOC2 evidence submission

Thanks Kimberly — technical notes / feasibility:
- Backup snapshots: we keep rolling snapshots; standard purge is 30/90/365 depending on storage tier. We can mark a subset of snapshots with a metadata flag ("audit_hold:carepath-202702") which prevents automatic purge for a configured window (up to 90 extra days). We can deliver a CSV manifest (backup_snapshot_map.csv) that maps snapshot ids -> tenant ids -> retention_until dates.
- Log retention: our logging tier supports retention policy overrides per-tenant for structured event logs. Extending to 18 months for structured auth/event logs is feasible if CarePath confirms the exact event types and agrees to the access controls Kimberly requested. We cannot extend retention for raw request payloads or personally-identifiable content without additional approvals.
- Deletion workflow: once the retention window expires we run a two-stage deletion: 1) tombstone + quarantine (30 days) to allow emergency replay, 2) irreversible purge. We can document rollback and emergency purge escape hatches in the runbook. I've attached our internal playbook excerpt for log-exception handling (redwood-playbook-log-exception.md).

Operational asks from CarePath: a signed addendum, list of auditor emails, and confirmation of the tenant IDs to flag. Also advise if you require a copy to be hosted (export) or just retained within Redwood's audit_hold snapshots.

—Rishi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-playbook-log-exception.md (MD), backup_snapshot_map.csv (CSV)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carepath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention needs for upcoming SOC2 evidence submission

Daniel — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps below (agreed items):

1) Scope: CarePath production tenant only; event-level auth and matching logs (no content/payload).
2) Backup snapshots: Redwood will tag specified snapshots with audit_hold, which will add up to +90 days to the snapshot purge window. We will provide backup_snapshot_map.csv showing snapshot ids and new retention_until dates.
3) Log retention: Temporary carveout to 18 months for structured auth/event logs only; no raw payloads.
4) Controls: limited auditor access (named auditors), audited exports only, hashed evidence artifacts.
5) DPA addendum: Kimberly attached DPA_Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf — please review. Once signed we will apply the flags. We can also place the addendum on DocuSign if you'd prefer (link below).

Requested from CarePath before we enact changes: signed addendum, list of auditor emails, and confirmation of tenant IDs to flag. If you provide those by EOD Feb 20 we will have the manifest and confirmation back to you within 3 business days.

Proposed brief call to finalize scoping tomorrow (Feb 19) — propose 9:00am PT or 1:00pm PT. Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Attachments: DPA_Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf, backup_snapshot_map.csv, redwood-playbook-log-exception.md
